source_contract.topic: Eigenvalues, Eigenvectors, and the Power Iteration

rationale: This is the foundational eigenpair definition; it introduces the mathematical objects used by all later items.
The characteristic equation is meaningful only after eigenvalues and eigenvectors have been defined.
The spectral decomposition presupposes the eigenpair definition and external knowledge of orthogonality and projection.
Magnitude ordering and uniqueness of the dominant eigenvalue require the eigenvalue concept but not the full spectral decomposition.
The update is motivated by the eigenpair relation and requires matrix-vector multiplication and non-zero-vector normalization.
The dominant-component derivation uses the symmetric eigenbasis expansion, magnitude ordering, and repeated power updates.

fallback_when_explanatory_dependencies_o.instruction: State the real-symmetric hypotheses, non-zero dominant projection, no-breakdown condition, and asymptotic rate without presenting the full eigenbasis derivation.

rationale: The result requires the magnitude gap and normalized iteration; the spectral theorem and component derivation explain rather than define the bounded convergence statement.

fallback_when_explanatory_dependencies_o.instruction: Explain sign equivalence of eigenvectors locally without the broader largest-magnitude comparison.

rationale: Sign alternation follows from a negative eigenvalue under the normalized update; RC-014 supplies useful but non-essential magnitude context.

fallback_when_explanatory_dependencies_o.instruction: Define the Rayleigh quotient for any non-zero vector before connecting it to power-iteration iterates.

rationale: The quotient uses the eigenpair concept and inner products; power iteration supplies its main application but is not needed for the definition.

fallback_when_explanatory_dependencies_o.instruction: Define the residual and its zero-eigenpair property without comparing residual stopping with sign-sensitive iterate differences.

rationale: The residual uses an eigenpair relation and Rayleigh estimate; the normalized iteration and sign ambiguity explain why it is preferable as a stopping measure.
The complete algorithm combines the normalized update, Rayleigh estimate, residual, breakdown check, tolerance, and iteration limit.

fallback_when_explanatory_dependencies_o.instruction: Use the eigenbasis coefficient statement to explain the missing projection without reproducing the complete convergence expansion.

rationale: The failure condition uses the symmetric eigenbasis, dominant eigenvalue, normalized update, and the dominant projection coefficient.

fallback_when_explanatory_dependencies_o.instruction: Explain tied dominant magnitude and slow convergence using the magnitude ratio without presenting the full component derivation.

rationale: The limitation depends on magnitude ordering and the iteration; the derivation and convergence result provide deeper justification of the ratio effect.
The distinction compares eigenvalues and therefore requires only the eigenpair definition.

fallback_when_explanatory_dependencies_o.instruction: State that the clean orthogonal real decomposition and bounded convergence explanation are restricted to the symmetric setting, without teaching the full symmetric proof.

rationale: The non-symmetric boundary contrasts with the symmetric spectral and convergence statements but can be taught as a concise scope limitation.
Input conversion, shape validation, non-zero checks, and initialization implement the normalized algorithm specification.
Runtime semantics implement the update, Rayleigh quotient, residual stopping, overall algorithm, and validated initialization.

fallback_when_explanatory_dependencies_o.instruction: Supply the exact eigenvalues as given and check the dominant estimate and residual without deriving the characteristic polynomial or revisiting the general magnitude distinction.

rationale: The worked result needs eigenpair and dominance concepts, Rayleigh and residual checks, and the runtime implementation; the characteristic equation and general comparison are explanatory.

external_prerequisite_concepts.name: Matrix-vector products
external_prerequisite_concepts.content_boundary: Interpret and compute A x for a real square matrix and a compatible vector; exclude matrix multiplication theory beyond what the Contract items use.
external_prerequisite_concepts.rationale: Eigenpair equations and every power update require matrix-vector multiplication.

external_prerequisite_concepts.name: Euclidean vector norms and normalization
external_prerequisite_concepts.content_boundary: Define the Euclidean norm, normalize a non-zero vector, and recognize zero-vector breakdown; exclude general normed-space theory.
external_prerequisite_concepts.rationale: Normalization and residual norms are operational requirements of the selected algorithm and implementation.

external_prerequisite_concepts.name: Orthogonality, orthonormal bases, and projection coefficients
external_prerequisite_concepts.content_boundary: Use inner products to explain orthonormal eigenvectors, basis expansion, and coefficients v_i^T x; exclude abstract inner-product-space theory.
external_prerequisite_concepts.rationale: The symmetric spectral expansion and missing-projection failure depend on orthogonal coordinates.

external_prerequisite_concepts.name: Determinants and characteristic polynomials
external_prerequisite_concepts.content_boundary: Interpret det(A-lambda I)=0 for small matrices; exclude symbolic algorithms for large characteristic polynomials.
external_prerequisite_concepts.rationale: RC-002 uses the characteristic equation as motivation but it is not needed for the iterative update itself.

external_prerequisite_concepts.name: Inner products and quadratic forms
external_prerequisite_concepts.content_boundary: Compute x^T A x, x^T x, and compatible scalar-vector expressions used by the Rayleigh quotient and residual; exclude general quadratic-form classification.
external_prerequisite_concepts.rationale: The Rayleigh quotient and its use in the residual require these operations.

external_prerequisite_concepts.name: Iterative algorithms, tolerances, and iteration limits
external_prerequisite_concepts.content_boundary: Interpret initialization, repeated updates, residual tolerance, early return, and maximum iterations; exclude convergence theory not already in the Contract.
external_prerequisite_concepts.rationale: The full algorithm and implementation semantics require control-flow understanding beyond the isolated update formula.

external_prerequisite_concepts.name: Basic NumPy vector operations
external_prerequisite_concepts.content_boundary: Use array conversion, shape inspection, matrix-vector multiplication, norms, comparisons, exceptions, and tuple returns needed by the Contract implementation; exclude unrelated NumPy APIs.
external_prerequisite_concepts.rationale: The implementation and worked runtime result require reading or writing the specified NumPy routine.
